correctedState: Split, and the split is real. SKILLS comply fully: runtime-skill-content.ts:497-600 expands $ARGUMENTS, $ARGUMENTS[N], bare $N and declared $name in one left-to-right pass, longest-match-at-a-position, with backslash escaping and no re-scan of substituted text; reached for /skill invocations via sessions.ts:334 -> runtimeSkillArguments (:607) -> base-agent.ts:2329. COMMANDS do not: sessions.ts:334 is the single expansion chokepoint for every non-MCP command source (native .nessy-agent/commands and .agents/commands, plugin prompt-commands, workflow commands) and it is one regex over /\$ARGUMENTS|\{\{args\}\}/g, so `/fix-issue 123` leaves a literal `$0`/`$1` in the body the model receives (modelMessage is handed straight to sendMessage at sessions.ts:373). Two refinements to the original finding. (a) The claim should be anchored to claude-directory.md:304 ('For positional access, use $0 $1 and so on', in the .claude/commands example) rather than :222, which is the skills sentence we already satisfy. (b) The plugin half is a DECLARED deferral, not a silent one: claude.ts:653-654/741-749 detects `$1`-`$9` in an imported command body and emits a `plugin.deferred.claude_command_dynamic_substitution` compatibility entry. That detection pattern is /\$[1-9]\b/, so it misses `$0` entirely, and native plus workflow commands get no deferral notice at all -- for those the placeholder fails silently. MCP prompt commands are correctly exempt: they map a quote-aware positional tail onto the prompt's declared parameters via mapMcpPromptArguments/getPrompt before the regex ever runs.
